1.title: How You Like That
1.listen: Pitch is how high or low a sound is. While it plays, pick out the lowest part (the bass) and the highest part (the voices). Two notes can share a letter name and still sit in different octaves.
1.guitar: Play A on the open A string, then the A an octave higher at fret 2 of the G string. Same letter, higher pitch: that's an octave.

2.title: On The Ground
2.listen: This song is in D♭ major, a key with five flats. Hum the note the chorus settles on. That's D♭, the first note of its major scale.
2.guitar: Put a capo on fret 1 and play the open C major scale (C D E F G A B C). The capo moves every note up a half step, so now you're playing the D♭ major scale.

3.title: Lovesick Girls
3.listen: The chorus loops D♯m, C♯, F♯ and B. All four chords fit the six-sharp key signature shared by D♯ minor and F♯ major, which are relative keys. Does the loop feel at home on D♯m (minor) or on F♯ (major)?
3.guitar: Put a capo on fret 4 and strum Bm, A, D and G. With the capo, those shapes sound as D♯m, C♯, F♯ and B.
